title: The C hello world, line by line (what each piece does)
description:
Everyone copies the six-line C hello world, but almost nobody explains what each line is for. This Short walks the "Anatomy of the program" breakdown from the C Mastery Path setup lesson: what including stdio.h does before compilation, why int main returns an exit status, what return 0 signals to the shell, and why gcc names your binary a.out when you forget the -o flag.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/c-mastery-path/level-1/01-setup/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Every C hello world has the same few pieces. Most tutorials make you copy them without saying what they do.
Here's the whole program. Six lines, no filler. And no class wrapper like in Java. C has no objects.
The include line is a preprocessor directive. It pulls in printf's declaration before compilation starts. Drop it, and the compiler doesn't know what printf is.
int main is the entry point. The int means it returns an integer exit status to the shell. Return zero means success, non-zero means an error.
Now compile it. The dash o flag names the output binary. Leave it off, and gcc just calls it a dot out.
That return zero isn't decoration. It's you telling the shell the program worked. Every piece earns its place.
The full anatomy table and exercise are in the lesson.
